was: City of Escondido campground above Dixon Lake. 45 sites for tents or RVs to 35 ft, about 10 full-hookup (30-amp) sites - most suit mid-size rigs; showers, dump. Reservable. --Claude

was: Medicine Bow NF campground on the Battle Highway (WY-70) 18 miles west of Encampment, ~8,800 ft. 13 back-in sites in the trees; the FS calls them small and for trailers under 22 ft, though the measured driveways run 25-99 ft - a 23-ft rig is at the stated edge. Vault toilet, no drinking water, no trash service, no hookups. Some sites reservable, season mid-June to September. Baby Lakes Trail into the Huston Park Wilderness across the highway. --Claude

was: Nebraska Game and Parks, Area 1 on the south shore of Branched Oak Lake northwest of Lincoln; Middle Oak Creek (Area 4) is a separate entry. Paved herringbone loops on an open grassy point and the shore: the east loop's front row (sites 43-49) ends about 20 m from the water across grass and a sandy strip, and the point's outer pads are 25-60 m from the riprapped shore. A middle loop of pads between the two is not on the booking site. --Claude

was: Rustic 52-site Wisconsin DNR campground in the southern Northern Highland-American Legion State Forest, on the southeast corner of Buffalo Lake near Woodruff. No hookups; three vault toilets and three hand pumps, sand beach and boat ramp. Pads are uneven - reviewers say take care over ~30 ft. Open about April 30 to Columbus Day. Reservable on the Wisconsin DNR system; state park vehicle admission sticker required. --Claude

was: Campground at 7231 S. M-88 near Bellaire in the Chain of Lakes area; concrete and gravel full-hookup sites (back-in and pull-through), water/electric back-ins, tent sites and cabins, with a pool. Boat parking allowed at some sites if the boat fits on the pad. --Claude

was: Franchise Jellystone Park in the woods outside Grayling.  A site may share its water and electric pedestal with another, so extension cords and extra hoses may be needed, and sewer sites are limited.  There is a pool (no lifeguard), a jumping pillow, mini golf, a Silent Disco (new in 2026) and a Bear Factory; day passes cost $15 a person, Sunday to Thursday, and early check-in $35.  The person booking must be 21 and a site holds one immediate family; e-bikes, EV charging and outside firewood aren't allowed, nor are golf carts for overnight guests.  Two dogs at most; quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m.  Cabins and RVs are rented. --Claude
